newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says he fears German political paralysis.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says he fears German political paralysis.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has expressed concern in a press interview that political paralysis in Germany is harming the planned launch of the European Union's single currency in 1999.

Prodi told the German weekly newspaper Welt am Sonntag that some leaders in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) were making a dangerous mistake by opposing Italy's participation in the currency in the first wave.

Prodi, eager to relieve German worries that the future currency the euro will not be as strong as the deutschemark, proposed that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer should be named to head the European Monetary Institute, the new EU central bank.
"I don't like Germany when it is as paralysed as it now is," Prodi said in the interview released ahead of publication on Sunday. "I am afraid of a Germany that is afraid."

Although most German leaders from the major parties firmly support economic and monetary union (EMU), opinion polls show a majority of Germans are opposed to the single currency, especially one that would include what many see as an unstable Italian lira.
"I would like to see Germany show its political strength again," Prodi told the paper. "Uncertainty is, more than anything else, harmful to the process of European integration."

The German government has stumbled from one impasse to another recently, as Kohl's CDU was thwarted by the junior coalition partners Free Democrats (FDP) or the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), which control the upper house of parliament.

Prodi was quoted as saying that the economies of Italy and all of Europe had suffered in the years since the Berlin Wall fell as the Bundesbank raised interest rates to fight inflation that accelerated after German unification in 1990.
"It was in order that we had to pay a price for that," said Prodi, who noted there were few complaints about that. "But now it is Germany's turn to understand the historical development."

Prodi said he was "very, very concerned that several important politicians" in Germany want to make Italy's participation in the euro currency a domestic political issue before the German general election which must be held next year.
Asked by Welt am Sonntag about his views on remarks attributed to members of Kohl's CDU who say Kohl would lose the next election if Italy joins EMU, Prodi replied:

"That is a serious and dangerous mistake. I have one goal -- that Italy joins the currency union and I have asked my country to make sacrifices for that. I have put my own career at stake. It is not right that the fate of Italy can be sacrificed for the careers of German politicans. That is a dangerous game."
Prodi said he was confident the euro would be launched soon, although he avoided a question about when the single currency would be introduced.
"I am sure the euro is our future," Prodi said. "In my view there isn't any other country in Europe that has demanded of its citizens more than Italy to make the country fit for the euro."
